extracted.intended_audience: NIH fellowship reviewers, fellowship applicants, mentors, and institutional training administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A predoctoral fellowship (training) research proposal containing research strategy (Aims, methods, statistics), sponsor/institution selection, training plan, and institutional RCR (Responsible Conduct of Research) requirements for an NIH-style fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A p-value < 0.05 will be considered statistically significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This threshold is applied across planned analyses (e.g., Two-sample Student’s T test, one-way ANOVA) and data will be analyzed in GraphPad Prism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical tests specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Two-sample Student’s T test for pairwise comparisons and one-way ANOVA for multi-group comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data will be analyzed using GraphPad Prism; specify test appropriate to experimental design (e.g., two-sample T for blood vs adipose comparisons, one-way ANOVA for reactivation groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow cytometry acquisition and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow cytometry data will be collected on a BD Fortessa and analyzed in FlowJo to identify eGFP+ infected cells and characterize phenotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If direct detection of eGFP is insufficient, amplify signal with anti-eGFP antibody or use RNA-Prime Flow Assay probes for IE-1 and IE-2 to identify infected cells by flow cytometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of replicating virus
rubrics_metrics.description: Replicative virus and reactivation will be quantified by plaque assay and by qPCR quantification of viral DNA and reverse-transcribed cDNA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All methods quantified at 7-8 days post reactivation treatment; positive control analyses (e.g., lungs) are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of validated molecular probes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of probes specific for Immediate Early gene-1 and -2 (IE-1 and IE-2) conjugated to a fluorophore for flow-based detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These next-generation RNA-Prime Flow Assay probes serve as a fallback when eGFP detection is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and group design for reactivation experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Infect 10 mice per three different treatments (30 total C57BL/6 mice) with 3x10^5 pfu by IP and allow infection for at least three months before reactivation treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three reactivation methods (pharmacological, radiation, tissue explants) will be compared; controls include uninfected mice and infected mice without intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and timecourse design for CD8 T cell kinetics
rubrics_metrics.description: Infect 56 C57BL/6 mice with 3x10^5 pfu by IP and sacrifice 8 mice at days 7, 14, 21, 30, 90, 150, and 300 post-infection to analyze tetramer-specific CD8 T cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time points selected to capture acute contraction and memory inflation; peripheral blood collected as positive control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and schedule for chemokine/cytokine analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Infect 40 C57BL/6 mice with 3x10^5 pfu; harvest adipose tissue from 8 mice at days 1, 2, 3, 7, and 100 post infection and culture half of tissue/SVF while freezing the other half for qPCR validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supernatants collected one day post-culture and assayed by Luminex (26-plex ProcartaPlex); significant molecules validated by qPCR and considered candidates for depletion/knockout follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include equivalent numbers of uninfected mice and mice infected for greater than three months without intervention as negative controls; positive controls will analyze lungs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls to be compared statistically against experimental groups using the specified tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reactivation methods defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Three methods of viral reactivation: (i) pharmacological (cyclophosphamide, CY), (ii) total-body gamma irradiation (single sub-lethal 6 Gy dose), and (iii) tissue culture explants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After radiation, mice will be treated with cotrimoxazole (240 mg/L) in drinking water for 8 days; tissue explant procedure adapted from prior protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallback strategies for negative results in Aim 1
rubrics_metrics.description: If adipose tissue is not a site of viral replication, conclude other signals attract CD8 T cells and determine these signals by adipose tissue culture explants; if infected cells cannot be identified by flow cytometry, use eGFP antibody amplification or RNA-Prime Flow Assay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CY alone fails to reactivate virus, try coupled immune suppression combining CY with depleting antibodies for CD8, CD4, and NK cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated results and interpretation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect macrophages at polarization extremes and endothelial cells to be infected (eGFP+); expectation that adipose tissue can be a reservoir for latent virus and show higher viral load after reactivation treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If virus is detected following reactivation, interpret adipose as a site of persistence and latency; if not detected, conclude adipose is not a site of mCMV latency under tested conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phenotypic and functional T cell analysis methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform phenotypic and intracellular cytokine staining of CD8 T cells by flow cytometry, include tetramer analyses, and determine markers for short-lived effector cell phenotype (CD62Llow, IL-7Rα−, IL-15Rβ−).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If expected memory inflation patterns are not observed, identify epitopes via ex vivo stimulation using K41 cells transfected with ORF library, brefeldin A incubation, and intracellular IFNγ staining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cytokine/chemokine candidate expectations and downstream testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect IL-6, TNFα, RANTES, CXCL12 to be upregulated in infected adipose compared to uninfected; correlate these molecules with T cell increase and plan receptor disruption (CCR5, CCR6) in future studies to test impact on migration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Luminex screening followed by qPCR validation; validated molecules will inform depletion/knockout experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental quantification timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify reactivation by plaque assay and qPCR at 7-8 days post reactivation treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent timing across samples for comparability; analyze in GraphPad Prism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research strategy structure (Aims, anticipated results, pitfalls/alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Aim should state hypotheses, methods, anticipated results, and explicit pitfalls and alternative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide fallbacks and contingencies for negative or unexpected results and explain how alternative experiments would still address the research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor selection justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a sponsor based on expertise relevant to proposed work, the size and facilities of the lab, collaborative environment, and mentoring record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific examples of mentor’s expertise, lab contributions to the field, collaborations, and why the institutional environment supports project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training plan coursework and seminar expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal coursework toward the Ph.D. in Immunobiology (list of required/elective courses) and participation in seminar series (IMB595/695) with at least annual presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation performance assessed on critical thinking, clarity, style, content and density by peers and faculty; list specific courses and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR (Responsible Conduct of Research) certificate requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH RCR Certificate requires a minimum of nine (9) hours of RCR instruction: Core Workshop 1.5 hrs plus five elective workshops totaling 7.5 hrs; up to 3 hours of supplemental instruction from faculty mentor(s) may count toward the elective requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must be initiated within 30 days of the post-award date and completed within one calendar year after the post-award date.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR instructional format constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 7.5 hours must be live instructional formats (workshops, academic course hours, face-to-face discussions). No more than 1.5 hours of supplemental online instruction may count toward the RCR Certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The University encourages as much live instruction as possible; specific workshop topics are listed (e.g., human subjects, animal research, ethics of authorship).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR tracking, verification, and compliance monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs are responsible for ensuring completion of RCR training; individuals must keep documentation; Office for Research and Discovery certifies the plan and verifies completion via UAccess Learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences of noncompliance include forfeiture of research funds and sanctions against future federal funding, in addition to institutional sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value statement for RCR
rubrics_metrics.description: RCR training promotes ethical professional values and behaviors beyond simply meeting regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages more hours than the minimum and frames RCR as promoting research integrity and professional excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and professional development expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainee should be exposed to departmental seminars, external visitors, membership in professional societies, and opportunities to attend advanced courses and meetings (present work in poster/oral format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details include expected seminar attendees, planned external course applications, and membership in relevant societies (e.g., American Aging Association).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research facilities and core resources availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide description of laboratory space, tissue culture rooms, vivarium capacity (e.g., space for 3,500 mice), ABSL-2/3 containment, and available core facilities (flow cytometry sorting, sequencing, electron microscopy, proteomics, irradiation sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of specific equipment available in-lab (CO2 incubators, microscopes, PCR machines, -80C freezers) and fee-for-service cores; emphasize that facilities support the proposed experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor/trainee interactions and oversight plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular laboratory meetings (weekly), progress meetings (at least biweekly), and thesis committee meetings (2-3/year) to oversee trainee progress; specify number of additional fellows to be supervised (two).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe frequency and nature of mentoring interactions and how they will support trainee development (increased meetings during manuscript/presentation prep).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor's track record and trainee outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Document mentor’s prior trainees, their career outcomes, and representative examples to support mentor’s capability to train successful fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sample names, positions, and institutions as evidence of successful mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant qualifications and evidence of independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should demonstrate prior training, experimental skill, originality of research ideas, and ability to write the application with minimal mentor input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include prior presentations, collaborations, and examples (e.g., work presented at conferences) as evidence of readiness for the fellowship.
